Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete ask so we can get this into our MSA/SOW redline cycle. Two items we need Redwood to confirm and provide language for:

Alyssa

Hi Alyssa —

Appreciate the clear ask and the SOW. We're happy to work through a tailored availability rider for HealthX. Quick summary / next steps from our side:

- Availability commitment: we can propose a 99.99% monthly availability target for your production workspace in the US region. We will propose a service-credit schedule tied to % monthly availability bands (we'll include a standard tiered credit schedule and an alternate limited-credit option if you're requesting lower financial exposure).

- Latency: we can include a P95 generation latency objective (<=150ms) for a defined request profile. We'll need to map that to the exact model(s) and sequence-length assumptions in the SOW (suggestion: pin to the model variant used in production and a 512-token budget for the P95 measurement).

- Evidence & telemetry: we can provide a copy of our latest SOC 2 Type II and a telemetry package that includes: monthly P50/P95/P99 latency percentiles, uptime % by region, token-level cost breakdown for the audited month, and alerting/incident timelines. We'll offer 30/90/365-day retention options for raw traces; longer retention can be added to the order form as a paid add-on.

I've attached a draft internal availability rider and an evidence checklist for you to review. Looping in Ben (AM) and Kim (Legal) and Monica (CS) to coordinate redlines and onboarding evidence.

Proposed timeline: 48–72 business hours to produce an MSA/SOW redline that includes the rider + evidence appendix. If procurement needs faster turnaround we can escalate.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the heads up. A few legal and operational notes for the draft rider:

1) Definition clarity: we need a clear definition of "availability" (e.g., percent of successful 2xx responses measured at the Redwood edge for tenant production workspace) and an explicit exclusion list (scheduled maintenance windows, force majeure, customer misconfiguration, model retraining windows beyond our control).

2) Measurement window: propose monthly measurement with a 30-day rolling lookback for crediting cadence. If HealthX requests calendar-month measurement, call that out as an optional alternate in the order form.

3) Credit cap and cure: add a maximum aggregate credit cap per 12-month period and a cure window for intermittent outages to avoid small transients triggering credits.

4) Latency SLA: Legal is generally reluctant to hard-commit low-latency P95 across all payloads. Suggest we offer a P95 objective with an explicit "test profile" definition and a carveout that allows fallback to an agreed performance verification run during onboarding.

5) Evidence: SOC 2 Type II is OK to share via NDA-protected link. For telemetry artifacts, send only aggregated percentiles and anonymized traces unless HealthX signs a data-sharing addendum.

Action: David, can your team confirm what exact telemetry artifacts we can package for the 30/90/365-day retention options? Monica, confirm onboarding timeline and whether CS will run an initial performance verification with HealthX test profile.

Kim
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks — we've reviewed internally and attached a redline-ready rider and an evidence appendix for HealthX's SOW. Highlights:

- Draft rider includes 99.99% monthly availability target for the specified production workspace (US region) with a tiered credit schedule and a 12-month credit cap.
- Latency is offered as a P95 objective with a clear test profile; we'll run a verification during onboarding to baseline P95 for your actual payloads.
- Evidence appendix lists the SOC 2 Type II link (NDA required), the telemetry package contents, and the retention add-on options (30/90/365-day).
- We included two alternate order-form clauses: (A) standard availability credit schedule, (B) reduced-credit pilot schedule (for POC pilots where HealthX prefers lower financial exposure).

Next steps: please confirm which alternate you'd like in the order form (A or B), and whether procurement wants us to attach the SOC 2 link under NDA now or after redline. Once you confirm, we'll send a redline of the MSA/SOW with the rider ready for your counsel.
